//: TypeScript covers everything server-side — platform, modules, shared, lib, and all 153 API routes. Nothing under src/ is JavaScript any more (07/10/2026): the 421 browser files under src/components and src/app were converted 05–06/10/2026, and src/proxy.js and src/lib/langCookie.js followed as .ts. allowJs and checkJs are left as they were only because removing them is its own change — it touches tsconfig.strict.json, which says it goes with them, and the checks CI runs. This line said the reverse ('TypeScript covers the document application only; the rest stays plain JavaScript') long after Wave 3 made it false. See tsconfig.strict.json, which grades every .ts/.tsx with noImplicitAny on.
//exclude: services/ is EXCLUDED because it is not this application. Each folder under it is a separately deployed program with its own package.json, its own dependencies and its own tsconfig — services/pg-gateway needs @google-cloud/cloud-sql-connector, which the app neither has nor should have. `include` here is `**/*.ts`, so without this line the app's typecheck grades a service against dependencies that are not in the app's node_modules and fails on imports that are perfectly correct where they live. `next build` was never affected (Next compiles only what src/app imports); `tsc` was.
